author: reek
body: The Narrator folds a definition's annotations into a narration block, and the fold is SELECTIVE: Rationale, Discovery and Doctrine narrate, while Invariant, Warning and Todo do not. That selection is the whole behaviour worth pinning, and it is exactly what the old body could not see -- it created one Annotation, printed its kind, and narrated nothing, so it passed with nothing behind it.

author: reek
body: So this feeds one annotation of every kind and asserts both halves: the three that narrate appear in the formatted output, and the three that do not are absent.

author: reek
body: The selection is enforced TWICE and in series -- `fold-narration` guards on `is-narration-kind`, and `add-narration-line` then dispatches on the kind and returns the block untouched for Invariant, Warning and Todo. So this pins the composite property rather than either site, and removing one guard alone changes nothing. Measured: with both removed, line-count goes to 4 and `warning` flips to yes. Do not read a green here as evidence that a particular guard is live.

author: reek
body: The formatted narration is threaded as a parameter rather than read from a top-level constant. A constant is rebuilt at every mention, so reading one seven times would run format-narration seven times.
